newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico aims for rise in coffee output, exports.
newsitem.headline: Mexico aims for rise in coffee output, exports.

text.p: Mexico is targeting coffee output of six million 60-kg bags for the 1997-1998 harvest, compared with 5.1 million bags harvested in the recently ended 1996-1997 harvest, Mexican Coffee Council president Ruben Castillo said on Thursday.
Exports should reach about five million 60-kg bags for the 1996-1997 season, compared to about 4.13 million bags as of the end of June, he said in an interview with Reuters.
"The goal is to increase production by one million 60-kg bags each year until 2000, and let it stabilize at eight million bags," Castillo said.
He estimated Mexico will export all but the about one million bags it consumes domestically per year.

The expansion is based on an expected better use of coffee plantations, he said. Mexico will subsidize a new smaller variety of plant, so that coffee growers can cultivate more coffee plants in the same space.
"In Mexico the average hectare has 1,340 plants, whereas modern coffee plantations have between 2,500 and 5,000 plants," Castillo said. "It means we are behind in technical terms."
